answer: An agent marketplace uses stake as the inlet to its trading harbor: each identity must lock 100 tokens for 30 days before it can bid for jobs. Signing up with a digital quill is cheap, but activating 1,000 fake agents requires locking 100,000 tokens. The contract checks each account’s bond before accepting bids, so creating more names cannot bypass the capital requirement. The attacker loses access to that capital for the full lock period.
